newsitem.title: DUBAI: ATFP gives $27 million credit line to Jordan.
newsitem.headline: ATFP gives $27 million credit line to Jordan.

text.p: The Arab Trade Financing Programme (ATFP) and Jordan on Sunday signed two deals granting a $27.7 million credit line to Amman to help refinance two purchases of barley from Syria.

The deals, spanning 18 months, were signed by Jassim al-Manai, chairman of the ATFP board of directors and chief executive officer and Jordan's Central Bank Governor Ziyad Fariz in Amman on Sunday, the agency said in a statement.
The ATFP has extended 11 credit lines to Jordan worth $103.4 million since it was set up in 1991 to develop and promote trade among Arab countries.
It is 50 percent owned by the Abu Dhabi-based Arab Monetary Fund and other institutions. It does not finance oil and gas, re-exports or used items.
